chapter: Early recordings and arrival in New York
title: Controversy over 'Loch Lomond' and the CBS radio program
summary: The swing treatment of the folk song caused controversy, with a station manager in Detroit objecting.

blocks.x: I remember seeing in a periodical called "Rhythm," a short article on you by Leonard Feather. Maybe it was one of the first things written by you -- I think he said first you

And then the decision to do 'Loch Lomond' came after that.
Claude actually thought that 'Annie Laurie' might be the one to click. I mean if you're looking for something to click. As it turned out, 'Loch Lomond' was the one.
And, of course, you know it became quite controversial.
Yes. We would turn off the -- at the time there was a program on CBS called 'The Saturday Swing Club,' and Claude got me on the program.

I sang 'Loch Lomond' and -- Leo Fitzpatrick, station manager in Detroit, cut it off the air right in the middle of the song because he said it was sacrilegious to swing a traditional song. And then, of course, the following week, we did 'Loch Lomond' and these things on this side in

New York. And they had a group in Chicago -- they had Ray Heatherton and Reese Stevens with a big orchestra and a choir and everything singing 'Loch Lomond', and 'A Brown Bird Singing' straight.
And I was in New York with a small combination, (shivering). It ran on for quite a while.
